---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Intangible Leverage Wedge
EXPRESSION: SUB(RATIO(lt, at), RATIO(lt, ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Book leverage overstates true leverage for firms whose knowledge capital is expensed rather than capitalized; the size of this measurement wedge identifies firms that only look financially fragile.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The signal is exactly the leverage overstatement caused by omitting a five-year R&D capital stock from the asset base, so it is zero for non-R&D firms and largest for levered intangible-intensive firms. If investors price stated leverage rather than economic leverage, these firms carry an unwarranted distress discount and earn higher subsequent returns. The wedge cannot be produced by either theme alone: it requires both liabilities and an intangible stock adjustment.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: R&D Driven Loss Illusion
EXPRESSION: MUL(INDICATOR(NEG(ib), 0), RATIO(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), COALESCE(xad, 0)), at))
HYPOTHESIS: Among firms reporting accounting losses (a classic distress marker), those whose losses are attributable to discretionary intangible investment are not economically distressed and are mispriced relative to genuine loss-makers.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The indicator restricts attention to the loss-making distress state, and within it the signal ranks firms by the intensity of expensed R&D and advertising that mechanically depresses reported income. Investors extrapolating negative earnings underreact to the investment nature of these losses, generating positive abnormal returns. Non-loss firms take the value zero, so the effect is purely conditional on the distress state.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Knowledge Capital Solvency Score
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(ADD(re, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), at), RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt))
HYPOTHESIS: A distress score built on intangible-adjusted retained earnings and intangible-adjusted earnings coverage of liabilities separates genuine fragility from accounting fragility better than standard solvency ratios.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Cumulative R&D expensing permanently depresses retained earnings and current income, mechanically pushing innovative firms into the low-Z-score region of standard distress models. Adding back the R&D stock to retained earnings and R&D flow to earnings before scaling by liabilities restores a solvency measure that reflects real repayment capacity. High values identify firms that are solvent in economic terms but classified as distressed by accounting metrics.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Acquired Intangible Leverage Fragility
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at)), RANK(RATIO(lt, at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Goodwill is purchased rather than internally generated intangible capital; when it is financed with debt it represents genuine fragility, not mismeasured knowledge capital.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Goodwill-heavy balance sheets provide no cash flow cushion and are prone to impairment exactly when leverage constraints bind, so the joint state of high goodwill and high liabilities marks real default risk rather than accounting distortion. This is the mirror image of the R&D case and should predict low returns, sharpening the distinction between accounting and economic distress within intangible-intensive firms. The product is only large when both conditions hold jointly.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: R&D Burn Liquidity Filter
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(che, oancf), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lct)))
HYPOTHESIS: Among R&D-intensive firms, the binding risk is funding the research program, so internal liquidity net of the annual R&D burn relative to current liabilities separates survivable innovators from fragile ones.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: R&D intensity alone is a weak return predictor because it mixes well-funded innovators with cash-burning firms facing financing risk; scaling cash plus operating cash flow net of the R&D outlay by current liabilities isolates who can self-finance the program. The product is high only for intangible-heavy firms with a genuine liquidity buffer, which should earn the intangible premium without bearing distress losses. Low values flag intangible-heavy firms whose apparent distress is real.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Levered R&D Retrenchment
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(lt, at)), RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Debt overhang forces genuinely fragile intangible firms to cut research intensity; a multi-year decline in R&D intensity combined with high leverage is a management-revealed signal of true financial distress.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Managers cut discretionary intangible investment only when funding is genuinely constrained, so the five-year downward trend in R&D-to-sales acts as a revealed-preference distress indicator that accounting ratios miss. Interacted with high liabilities it identifies firms whose knowledge capital is depreciating precisely when they need it most, predicting low future returns. Conversely, low values correspond to levered firms that sustain research intensity, which the market underprices.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
